# Brāhmaṇadhammayāga Sutta (Iti 100 (It 4.1 PTS It 101))

**ID:** Iti 100 (It 4.1 PTS It 101)
**Section:** Itivuttaka (iti)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-2
**Title (Pali):** Brāhmaṇadhammayāga Sutta
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** The Holy Offering of the Teaching
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/iti100
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0504m.mul3.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Brāhmaṇadhammayāga Sutta* is the opening discourse of the fourth section of the *Itivuttaka* (Iti 100, It 4.1, PTS It 101) [SuttaCentral]. In this discourse, the Buddha depicts himself as a doctor and characterizes his monastic disciples as true heirs in the Dhamma rather than heirs in material things [SuttaCentral]. In secondary scholarship, Richard S. Cohen notes that the sutta contains imagery of the Buddha's legitimate or "breast-born" (*aurasa*) son, presenting a parallel formulation to the *Aggañña Sutta* (DN 27), wherein the Buddha rejects Brahmanical claims of spiritual sovereignty from Brahmā's mouth by asserting that his disciples are born of the Dhamma [Cohen, Śākyabhikṣus].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral identify resembling passages in the *Sela Sutta* of the *Majjhima Nikāya* (MN 92) and the *Sutta Nipāta* (Snp 3.7), while also noting citations of this text in the *Milindapañha* (Mil 5.3.10, Mil 5.5.3, and Mil 5.5.8) [SuttaCentral]. Computational text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus indicates extensive internal Pali parallels, showing substantial shared segments with the *Aṅguttara Nikāya*—most prominently the *Dukanipāta* (AN 2) and *Catukkanipāta* (AN 4), along with the *Dasakanipāta* (AN 10) and *Navakanipāta* (AN 9) [DharmaNexus]. Within the *Itivuttaka*, DharmaNexus records shared text with the *Dāna Sutta* (Iti 98) and the *Sabrahmaka Sutta* (Iti 106), while also confirming shared material with the *Aggañña Sutta* (DN 27) [DharmaNexus]. Outside Pali, DharmaNexus aligns segment §3.2 with the Tibetan *Abhidharmasamuccayavyākhyā* (D4054) [DharmaNexus]. The text has been translated into multiple languages, including English translations by Bhikkhu Sujato and John D. Ireland [SuttaCentral; Cohen, Śākyabhikṣus].
